knowledge:
- key_parameters: mat=Numeric matrix of data with samples in rows and features in columns ;; Y=Alternative matrix argument name when grouping factor x is not supplied ;; x=Grouping factor or vector representing experimental groups ;; B=Number of resamples to run (e.g., 5e1 or 1e2L) ;; test=Custom test function accepting response and grouping variables ;; distFun=Distribution function for transforming custom test statistics to z-values ;; zValues=Logical indicating whether to operate on the z-value scale (default TRUE) ;; resamZvals=Logical indicating whether to use the same resampling instances for marginal null distributions ;; groupName=Character string specifying the grouping variable name in a phyloseq object ;; FCname=Character string specifying the flow cytometry variable name in a phyloseq object
- alternatives: Standard Wilcoxon rank-sum or t-tests without resampling, which fail to account for test correlation and may suffer from reduced power or inflated false discovery rates under dependence.
- when_to_use: Use when performing simultaneous testing on highly correlated features, such as microbiome differential abundance analysis where compositional data is scaled by total cell counts.
- pitfalls: Setting zValues = FALSE to run the procedure on the scale of original test statistics (when the null distribution is unknown) may be numerically less stable.

workflows.name: matrix_simultaneous_inference
workflows.intent: Perform simultaneous hypothesis testing on a data matrix while accounting for test correlation using a collapsed null distribution.
workflows.stages: 1. Run simultaneous inference using reconsi ;; 2. Extract estimated tail-area false discovery rates and proportion of true nulls ;; 3. Plot the estimated null distribution ;; 4. Plot the approximate covariance matrix of test statistics
workflows.code:
fdrRes = reconsi(mat, x)
estFdr = fdrRes$Fdr
fdrRes$p0
plotNull(fdrRes)
plotApproxCovar(fdrRes)

workflows.name: phyloseq_differential_abundance
workflows.intent: Perform differential abundance analysis on a phyloseq object incorporating flow cytometry cell counts to account for correlation.
input: Vandeputte (phyloseq object containing microbiome abundance data and sample metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Run differential abundance analysis using testDAA ;; 2. Extract and summarize the estimated tail-area false discovery rates
workflows.code:
testVanDePutte = testDAA(Vandeputte, groupName = "Health.status", FCname = "absCountFrozen", B = 1e2L)
FdrVDP = testVanDePutte$Fdr
quantile(FdrVDP)
